context: 12-panel small multiples (4×3 grid, one per month) showing daily energy consumption overlaid across 3 years (2022–2024), with a shared global y-scale, synchronized crosshair interaction, and a 3-color year palette
first_impression: Clean, well-structured grid that reads immediately as a calendar — the seasonal U-shape (high winter/summer, low spring/fall) is apparent at a glance.
what_works: Shared global y-scale across all 12 panels enables direct cross-month comparison of absolute kWh values, which is the core insight; y-axis only on the left column and x-axis only on the bottom row eliminate redundant ink without losing reference.
what_doesnt: The three year-lines overlap heavily within each panel due to high noise amplitude (~12 kWh jitter vs ~4 kWh year-over-year trend), making year-on-year differences nearly impossible to read without the crosshair tooltip; the synchronized crosshair updates all 12 panels simultaneously, which is visually impressive but cognitively demanding — tracking 36 dots across 12 cells at once exceeds working memory.
